title: Perimeter forwarder + tracing orchestration for private deployments
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Design and implement a light-weight perimeter forwarder + tracing orchestration layer for Dedicated and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments to provide safe multi-tenant isolation, bounded egress, and low-overhead tracing hooks that integrate with Redwood Console dashboards.

Background: Current on-prem/VPC installs run a variety of collector agents and sidecars that can be heavy or require tenant-scoped configuration. We need a small, configurable forwarder that sits at the customer perimeter (host/NAT gateway or sidecar) that: 1) normalizes traces/metrics/logs to our ingest format, 2) attaches tenant-scoped metadata for RBAC and filtering, 3) enforces sampling/prefix-caching rules to protect bandwidth, and 4) orchestrates trace context propagation for high-cardinality request paths across private clusters.

Scope: This ticket covers design, a reference implementation in Go (light binary <25MB), integration tests, and a canary rollout plan for dedicated customers. It excludes full replacement of existing collectors and long-term migration of older on-prem agents (tracked under obs-migration project).

Design decisions and trade-offs considered:
- Push vs Pull: Push model from forwarder to our secure egress endpoint to ensure timely backpressure handling. Pull would require more customer-facing infra.
- Single binary vs sidecar + daemonset: Single binary with optional systemd/service support keeps footprint minimal; sidecar mode will be validated for k8s clusters.
- Sampling and prefix caching: Implement adaptive sampling rate per-tenant with configurable upper/lower bounds to prevent overload. Add lightweight prefix/KV cache for frequent request traces to reduce token churn across network.
- Tenant metadata attachment: Prefer adding tenant-id headers and a signed attestation token (short-lived) for the platform to enforce isolation; avoid sending raw tenant configs.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end trace appears in Redwood Console within 5s for a private deployment (99th percentile for internal test harness).
- Forwarder binary <25MB and memory <120MB under steady-state for 500 rps lab workload.
- Tenant isolation validated: traces/metrics from tenant A are never visible to tenant B in sandbox tests (automated multi-tenant e2e test).
- Sampling controls honored and adjustable via remote config (rollout config service) without forwarder restart.
- Integration test coverage: unit tests, integration with opentelemetry collector shim, and a k8s daemonset smoke test.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design doc & threat model (Confluence) + proto for metadata headers (week 1)
2) Reference forwarder in Go + simple CLI and k8s manifests (week 2)
3) Opentelemetry shim and trace-context propagation tests (week 3)
4) Performance tuning (batching, backoff, TLS handshake reuse) and CI benchmarks (week 4)
5) Canary rollout with two Dedicated customers and one on-prem partner; monitoring dashboard + rollback runbook (week 5)

Rollout and monitoring:
- Add dedicated dashboard in Console: per-tenant ingress latency, dropped traces, sampling rate, and egress bandwidth.
- Configure alerts: >1% dropped traces for 5m, egress >85% of configured bandwidth quota.

Security/Compliance notes:
- Forwarder will support customer-managed TLS certificates (SNI) and optional HSM-backed signing for attestation tokens.
- Will require an internal security review; initial threat model in Confluence linked below.
comments: 2026-02-25 Aisha Kapoor: Created ticket after architecture review with Infra and Runtime teams. Initial design doc link added.
2026-03-02 Ravi Singh: Spike complete for Go prototype. Memory envelope looks promising (~70MB at 200rps). Pushed prototype to github: https://github.com/redwood-inference/obs-forwarder/pull/12

2026-03-05 Design feedback from Emma Liu: suggested adding signed tenant attestation instead of raw tenant header; updated design doc to include attestation flow. See Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Perimeter+Forwarder+Design
2026-03-08 Security review kickoff with Priya Shah: flagged threat of replay attacks on sampling control messages; plan to use nonce+timestamp on remote config updates.
2026-03-12 Performance note from bench team: batching window of 15ms gives best tail-latency vs throughput tradeoff for small payloads; updating benchmark scripts.

2026-03-14 Ravi Singh: Started k8s daemonset smoke tests. Discovered edge-case where trace-context is dropped when request crosses a custom ingress controller; added mitigation to inject context into X-Forwarded-For chain.
